title: Why Do Cats Usually Land on Their Feet?
hook: A falling cat can rotate its body in midair even with almost no time to react.

title: How Do Fireflies Glow?
hook: A firefly makes light with a chemical reaction that wastes very little energy as heat.

title: Why Do Boats Float?
hook: A steel ship can float because its shape changes how much water it displaces.

title: How Noise-Cancelling Headphones Work
hook: Noise-cancelling headphones fight sound with another carefully timed sound wave.

title: Why Metal Feels Colder Than Wood
hook: Metal and wood can be the same temperature and still feel completely different to your hand.

title: How Induction Cooktops Heat a Pan
hook: An induction cooktop can stay relatively cool while the pan itself becomes the heater.

title: Why Soap Removes Grease
hook: Soap works because one end of its molecules likes water while the other end grabs oil.

title: Why Popcorn Pops
hook: A popcorn kernel is a tiny pressure vessel with water trapped inside.

title: How a Refrigerator Moves Heat
hook: A refrigerator does not create cold—it moves heat out of the cabinet.

title: Why Bubbles Are Round
hook: Bubbles become round because a sphere uses the least surface area for a given volume.

title: How Touchscreens Know Where You Touch
hook: Your phone screen can detect a finger without any button moving at all.

title: How Fiber-Optic Cables Carry Data
search: fiber optic total internal reflection data
hook: Internet data can travel through glass as pulses of light.

title: Why Static Electricity Makes Hair Stand Up
hook: Your hair can stand up because neighboring strands end up carrying similar electric charge.

title: How a Microphone Turns Sound Into Electricity
hook: A microphone begins with something incredibly small: a surface vibrating with the air.

title: Why Ocean Tides Happen
hook: The Moon pulls on the whole Earth, but the oceans reveal that pull most visibly.

title: How QR Codes Still Work When Damaged
hook: A QR code can lose part of its pattern and still be readable because redundancy is built in.

title: Why Airplane Windows Are Rounded
hook: Rounded airplane windows help spread stress instead of concentrating it at sharp corners.

title: How GPS Finds Your Position
hook: Your phone can estimate its position by comparing timing signals from several satellites.

title: Why Mirrors Seem to Reverse Left and Right
hook: A mirror does not actually swap left and right—it reverses the direction facing the mirror.

title: How Wi-Fi Carries Data Through the Air
hook: Wi-Fi sends digital information by changing radio signals too fast for us to notice.
